content: This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the potential benefits to you outweigh the risks of side effects. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. However, this is not an exhaustive list of possible side effects. If you are in the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. Similarly, if you are in Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Precautions: Before using ketoconazole, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other azole antifungals (such as clotrimazole, econazole, or miconazole), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is not known whether this drug passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription drugs, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Overdose: This medication may be harmful if swallowed. If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition. Do not use it later for another skin condition unless directed by your doctor. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature. This product is flammable; do not store or use it near an open flame. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This document provides a summary and does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Uses: This medication is used to treat a specific skin condition called seborrheic dermatitis, a type of dandruff. This condition is believed to be caused by a fungal infection (Malassezia furfur) of the skin or scalp, leading to dry, flaky skin (scales) on areas such as the scalp, face, ears, chest, or upper back. How to Use: Read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist before starting ketoconazole and each time you get a refill. Use this medication only on the scalp and skin. Clean and thoroughly dry the area to be treated. Wash your hands before and after applying the medication. Apply it to the affected skin and a small amount of the surrounding normal skin as directed by your doctor, usually once daily. The duration of treatment depends on your response to the medication and is typically around two weeks. Do not apply this medication more frequently than prescribed. Avoid contact with the eyes, nose, or mouth. If accidental contact occurs, rinse thoroughly with water. Use this medication regularly to achieve the best results. Do not wash the treated area for at least three hours after application. Side Effects: Burning, redness, or dryness of the treated skin may occur. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has judged that the benefit to you is greater than the risk of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. If you are in the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. If you are in Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
